key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL or chronic/recurrent over weeks to months. Not sudden. LOCATION: EPIGASTRIC, midline upper abdomen. No radiation typically. DURATION: Episodes last minutes to hours. May be constant in severe cases. CHARACTER: BURNING or GNAWING quality. Aching or hunger-like discomfort. AGGRAVATING: DUODENAL ulcers worsen 2-5 hours after meals (empty stomach). GASTRIC ulcers worsen WITH food. NSAIDs worsen. RELIEVING: DUODENAL ulcers improve WITH food and ANTACIDS. GASTRIC ulcers may improve with antacids but worsen with food. TIMING: EPISODIC with meal-related pattern. NOCTURNAL pain (wakes patient at night) is characteristic. DUODENAL=better with food, GASTRIC=worse with food. SEVERITY: 5-8/10, moderate. Not usually severe unless perforation. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Nausea, bloating, early satiety. NO vomiting unless obstruction. KEY POSITIVES: Meal-related pattern, antacid relief, nocturnal pain, NSAID use, H. pylori history. KEY NEGATIVES: SUDDEN SEVERE pain suggests perforation. Hematemesis (vomiting blood) or melena (black tarry stools) indicates bleeding ulcer needing urgent care. Weight loss suggests gastric cancer.
